methods.label: Find the edge midpoints and divide the section into triangles
methods.explanation:
Let \(O\) be the center of the octahedron. Central symmetry exchanges the two opposite faces, so the plane through \(O\) parallel to these faces divides the octahedron into equal volumes. Moving this plane parallel to itself would increase one volume and decrease the other. Since congruent solids have equal volumes, the given cutting plane must pass through \(O\).

The three vertices of one parallel face lie equally far above this plane, and the three vertices of the opposite face lie equally far below it. Thus the six edges joining the two faces meet the cutting plane at their midpoints. The section is a convex hexagon, with one side in each of the other six triangular faces. Each side joins two edge midpoints of a unit equilateral triangle, so the triangle midsegment theorem gives section side length \(1/2\).

To calculate the area, we also need the distance from \(O\) to each section vertex. View the octahedron as two congruent square pyramids joined along a unit square. That square has half-diagonal \(1/\sqrt2\). Each apex is distance \(1\) from its base vertices, so its height above the square is also \(\sqrt{1-1/2}=1/\sqrt2\). Therefore every octahedron vertex is distance \(1/\sqrt2\) from \(O\).

If \(M\) is the midpoint of any edge \(UV\), then \(OU=OV\), so \(OM\perp UV\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
OM=\sqrt{\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)^2-\left(\frac12\right)^2}=\frac12.
\]
Consequently, joining \(O\) to consecutive vertices of the section produces six equilateral triangles of side \(1/2\). Because \(O\) lies inside the convex section, these triangles cover it without overlapping interiors.

Each triangle has height \(\sqrt3/4\), so the section area is
\[
6\left(\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right)=\frac{3\sqrt3}{8}.
\]
Here \(3\) and \(8\) are relatively prime, and the radicand \(3\) is squarefree. Hence \(a+b+c=3+3+8=\boxed{14}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
